outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms in writing that the mezzanine is not a second story and the district use count is below 179, proceed with entity formation, business registration and a fictitious business name filing. What to say: File LLC Articles of Organization with the California Secretary of State ($70), obtain a federal EIN from the IRS (free, same day online), register the business with SF Treasurer & Tax Collector (Business Registration Certificate, $55–$700 tiered by gross receipts, 1–5 days), and file a fictitious business name statement with the SF County Clerk if the public name differs from the LLC name ($60–$120, then publish once a week for four weeks and file proof within 45 days). These are prerequisites for the health permit, building permit and all other City applications.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms the mezzanine is not a second story and the use count is below 179, file a Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning Department for a first-story restaurant in NCT-MISSION. What to say: State that the restaurant occupies 3,953 sq ft on the first story and mezzanine (confirm the mezzanine is not counted as a second story per the pre-application meeting), serves 120 seats, operates a full commercial kitchen with hood, serves no alcohol, and closes before midnight. Emphasize that the concept is not formula retail (or disclose if it is), that the operator will appoint a community liaison and commit to sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius, soundproofing to Noise Ordinance standards, odor control equipment, and keeping garbage indoors except during pickup. Attach a floor plan, equipment layout, and a narrative explaining how the restaurant meets the conditional-use findings in Planning Code Section 303. Budget $3,100–$15,000 in CUA fees (depending on construction cost) and 4–8 months to a hearing.
outcomes.note: Records show only that NCT-MISSION applies but state restaurant permission is 'unknown'; no fees, timelines, thresholds, or requirements are given.

outcomes.original: Filing step: In parallel with the CUA application, submit stamped architectural plans for tenant improvements and a DPH plan check to San Francisco Department of Building Inspection and Department of Public Health. What to say: Hire an architect licensed in California who has completed restaurant plan checks in San Francisco. Submit two sets of scaled drawings showing the kitchen layout, hood and suppression system, hand sinks, prep surfaces, restrooms, ADA access, and all equipment; route the building permit application to Planning (for zoning sign-off once the CUA is approved), DPH (for health plan check), Fire (for Place of Assembly permit and hood inspection if occupant load is 50+), and SFPUC (for grease interceptor if cooking). Pay the DPH plan-check fee ($2,207 for new restaurant, eight hours review) and the building permit fee (percentage of construction valuation, estimate $800–$15,000). The DPH review takes 21–60 days; schedule a pre-final inspection at 80% construction complete.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After the Planning Commission approves the CUA, obtain the Motion with conditions, then apply for the health permit to operate and schedule the DPH pre-opening inspection. What to say: Submit the health permit application online with the Business Account Number, Location ID, federal EIN, and the name and certificate number of the on-staff certified food safety manager (obtain a ServSafe or equivalent ANSI-accredited certificate within 60 days of opening, $100–$250, 1–14 days). Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (includes initial inspection); the annual license fee for restaurants is $0 for FY2026–28. The pre-opening inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans, all equipment is installed and functioning, hand sinks and hot water are available, surfaces are sealed, and garbage receptacles are in place. Failed inspections push openings by 2–3 weeks, so walk the space against the DPH checklist a week before the scheduled inspection.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Before opening, register for state and local taxes, obtain workers' compensation insurance, enroll employees in RBS and food handler training, and secure ASCAP and BMI licenses for recorded music. What to say: File for a California Seller's Permit with CDTFA (free, 1–14 days online) and register as an employer with EDD if you have employees (free, 1–7 days, needs the EIN). Obtain workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund (mandatory from the first employee; premiums are 2–6% of payroll for restaurant class codes). Each employee who handles food must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire ($7–$15, online, one day), and each alcohol server and manager must complete RBS certification within 60 days ($3 registration + $10–$25 course). Subscribe to ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses for recorded music ($300–$2,500 per year each, formula-based on occupancy and music use, 1–7 days online). Set up organics (green bin) collection with the City hauler per SB 1383.
